name: Google Cloud TPU v6e (Trillium)
memory_bandwidth_basis: Vendor-published per-chip HBM bandwidth of 1638 GBps; memory generation and bus width not stated in the spec table.
notes: Per-chip figures. Google calls out 'Performance/total cost of ownership (expected) 1' as a published spec row, i.e. the headline claim is a ratio against v5e rather than a raw number. Unlike v5p, v6e does publish INT8 = 2x BF16 (1836 TOPS vs 918 TFLOPS), so v6e restored the int8-doubling that v4 did not have. 32 GB HBM at 1638 GB/s gives 560 FLOP/byte BF16, the highest compute-to-byte ratio of any Google part here, so v6e is the first TPU where larger batch prefill actually becomes compute-feasible rather than purely bandwidth-limited. Two MXUs per TensorCore (down from four on v4/v5p/v5e), which shifts the weight-stationary geometry rather than the totals. Pod = 256 chips on a 2D torus, ICI 800 GBps bidirectional per chip with 4 ports, plus SparseCore units for embedding-style irregular access. v6e-8 is a full-host 8-chip slice explicitly optimised for single-workload inference.
